$comment: Lanternlight Claude Code settings. Windows paths MUST use forward slashes - a single backslash makes this file invalid JSON, and an unparseable settings file registers no hooks and warns about nothing. The PreToolUse matcher MUST name every shell tool that can reach git: this machine is PowerShell-primary, and a matcher of 'Bash' alone let a commit issued through the PowerShell tool bypass the gate entirely. Measured 2026-08-09. Attribution is BLANKED, not merely unset: CLAUDE.md forbids a Co-Authored-By trailer as operator policy, and the harness injects one by default. Both the current key (attribution.commit) and the deprecated one (includeCoAuthoredBy) are set, because an older client reads only the latter and would reintroduce the trailer silently. Set 2026-09-06. The SessionStart hook runs ops/inbox_watch.py for ROADMAP OPS-33, and it deliberately differs from the other two in two ways: it uses python.exe rather than pythonw.exe, because the session must SEE its stdout and pythonw suppresses the console, and it carries NO matcher, because an omitted matcher runs on every start while a matcher regex that fails to match is a hook that silently never fires. Added 2026-09-06 with operator approval. The second PostToolUse entry runs tools/syntax_check_hook.py for ROADMAP OPS-37: it compiles each edited .py and reports an unparseable file on stderr at the moment it is written, because a hook interpreter here is windowless and a broken file is otherwise silent until a much later test run. It carries an EXPLICIT matcher rather than none - an omitted matcher fires on every tool, including Read and Bash, where there is nothing to compile - and it names NotebookEdit alongside Edit and Write because the hook also reads notebook_path. It exits 0 on every path by design; a PostToolUse hook that exits non-zero breaks the session it runs in. It uses python.exe rather than the pythonw.exe of the two hooks above, so its report is not routed through an interpreter chosen for having no console; the accepted cost is the same one the SessionStart hook already pays. Added 2026-09-07. The UserPromptSubmit hook runs ops/inbox_watch.py --on-prompt for ROADMAP OPS-41: it acknowledges the inbox ONCE per session on the operator's own turn, which is the event SessionStart cannot be - SessionStart fires for subagents too and a hook on it cannot tell them apart. It carries NO matcher, because UserPromptSubmit takes none and a matcher regex that fails to match is a hook that silently never fires. It uses pythonw.exe and prints nothing on every path, because a UserPromptSubmit hook's stdout is injected into the session context; and it exits 0 on every path, because exit code 2 on this event BLOCKS the operator's prompt. Added 2026-09-07.
